question.text: Per the December 2025 NISM Series I workbook, which statement about STT (Securities Transaction Tax) on exchange-traded currency derivatives (ETCD) is correct?

answer.text: STT is levied on ETCD transactions at the same rate as on equity derivatives
STT is levied on ETCD only on the buyer of options
STT is levied on ETCD only on the seller of futures
STT is currently not applicable on ETCD transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: The December 2025 NISM Series I workbook lists the statutory levies applicable to ETCD transactions but states that STT is currently not applicable on ETCD transactions. GST and stamp duty may apply as statutory levies on ETCD transactions, but STT itself is not currently charged. The Trap: Candidates often assume STT applies to every exchange-traded derivative because they remember it on equity F&O. The workbook draws an explicit line for the currency segment: STT is not currently applicable on ETCD. Note: The position is a function of current statutory law as captured by the workbook; tax rates and applicability can change, so always confirm against the current edition before quoting in a client document.
